body:
The Lua provider in `koreader/plugins/cwasync.koplugin/kobo_sqlite_provider.lua`
duplicates the colour table that finding F-5769c9 measured as wrong, and it was
NOT fixed alongside the server in the F-5769c9 PR. It still holds:

    local COLOR_NAME_TO_INT = { yellow = 0, red = 1, green = 2, blue = 3 }
    local COLOR_INT_TO_NAME = { [0] = "yellow", [1] = "red", [2] = "green", [3] = "blue" }

against the measured device mapping (Kobo Clara BW 4.45.23792):

    0 yellow / 1 pink / 2 blue / 3 green / 4 grey

So the plugin, running on-device, has the same three defects the server had:
no entry for 4 (every organic highlight on a greyscale device reads back as
"yellow"), 2 and 3 swapped, and 1 called "red" — a colour Kobo does not have.
`koboIntToColorName` additionally defaults an out-of-range code to "yellow",
which is the invented-colour pattern the server side removed.

WHY IT WAS SPLIT OUT RATHER THAN FIXED IN THE SAME PR. The fix itself is small
and was written and passing (`lua tests/device_annotations_test.lua`), but
`tests/unit/test_cwasync_plugin_version_bump_gate.py` requires any change to
the plugin to bump `_meta.lua` + `main.lua` to "the version being cut", which
it reads from the newest DATED CHANGELOG section. On a feature branch that
section is the version already tagged (4.1.38 at the time of writing), so the
only declaration that makes CI green is one that has already been published —
and publishing a *different* plugin under an already-shipped version is worse
than the bug. The gate's own docstring says a declaration no release will ship
"offers devices an update that does not exist".

The consequence is structural, not specific to this fix: any PR that touches
the plugin outside a release cut cannot go green. Plugin changes have to ride
with the release train, which dates the new section and bumps both Lua files in
the same commit.

FIX SHAPE when it is picked up (mirror cps/services/annotation_colors.py):

    local COLOR_NAME_TO_INT = { yellow = 0, pink = 1, blue = 2, green = 3, grey = 4, gray = 4 }
    local COLOR_INT_TO_NAME = { [0] = "yellow", [1] = "pink", [2] = "blue", [3] = "green", [4] = "grey" }

* `colorNameToKoboInt` cannot answer "unknown" — the column takes an integer —
  so "red" and anything unrecognised degrade to 0 (yellow), deliberately NOT to
  pink, which would silently claim the device reproduced it.
* `koboIntToColorName` should return nil for an unmeasured code, which omits
  `color` from the portable annotation; the server then reads "no colour
  supplied" instead of inventing yellow.
* The test at `tests/device_annotations_test.lua::testColorMapping` pins the
  OLD table and has to be rewritten with it.

NOT HARDWARE-VERIFIED either way: the mapping is measured (F-5769c9), but the
plugin's own read/write round trip against a device was not exercised.

--- THE BLOCK IS STILL LIVE, RE-MEASURED 2026-08-22 (not inherited from the filing) ---

OBSERVED on main at 53956cc70:

    newest dated CHANGELOG section : v4.1.39 - 2026-08-21
    newest git tag                 : v4.1.39
    plugin declares                : 4.1.39 in both _meta.lua and main.lua

The gate derives "the version being cut" from the newest DATED changelog section.
Today that section is v4.1.39, which is already tagged and published. So a PR that
changes plugin substance outside a release cut can only go green by declaring a
version that has already shipped -- which is the exact failure the gate exists to
prevent ("offers devices an update that does not exist"). The block is structural
and it is real right now, not merely historical.

The unblocking event is the pre-tag bookkeeping commit that rolls a NEW dated
section. Until then the plugin lane is closed, and cutting a release to open it is
a release-train decision rather than something a fix should trigger for itself.

QUEUED BEHIND THIS BLOCK, and both are device-side highlight safety:
  F-0eb843  wrong colour table -- every organic highlight on a greyscale device
            reads back as "yellow"; 2 and 3 swapped; "red" is a colour Kobo has not
  F-6d6dfd  the "couldn't read the local set" guard is a constant true on the
            default provider, so a failed read is indistinguishable from an empty
            one at the callsite that decides what to delete

  F-e4da4d  the delete client half -- CWASyncClient.lua sends the whole deletion
            id list in one request under a 15s timeout, unbatched and uncapped,
            so an oversized delete cycle fails entirely rather than partly

Recorded together so the next release cut picks up both rather than rediscovering
each separately.

--- CORRECTION 2026-08-22: THIS FINDING WAS ALREADY FIXED, AND MY 2026-08-22 QUEUE NOTE ABOVE OVERSTATED IT ---

I filed the queue note above claiming this defect was live and blocked behind a
release cut. That was wrong, and it was wrong in the direction that inflates
urgency, so it is corrected here rather than quietly dropped.

OBSERVED on main at 0b8c2d02d: the colour table is already correct --
COLOR_NAME_TO_INT has pink=1, blue=2, green=3, grey=4/gray=4, and
COLOR_INT_TO_NAME has [4]="grey". koboIntToColorName returns nil for an
unmeasured code rather than defaulting to yellow. Fixed by #1752 (1c215cbc1,
2026-08-19), one day AFTER this finding was filed.

There is also a deliberate later refinement the finding's own fix shape
contradicts: `WRITE_ONLY_NEAREST = { red = 1 }` maps a web-reader red to pink on
WRITE, one-directionally, because pink is the nearest colour the device actually
has and Color=1 always reads back as "pink". The finding said red should degrade
to 0/yellow. The shipped decision is better -- yellow is a colour the Kobo really
does have, so degrading red to yellow misrepresents the highlight as a different
real colour, while pink at least names what the device is showing. A change
implementing this finding's letter was written on
fix/plugin-highlight-safety-trio and REVERTED for exactly this reason.

Resolving as already-fixed. The lesson is the one the memory index already
carries: a finding records what was true when it was written, and the fix may
have landed between the filing and the reading.
title: The KOReader cwasync plugin carries the same wrong Kobo colour table the importer had

resolution.note: Already fixed by #1752 (2026-08-19), one day after this was filed. Colour table is correct and koboIntToColorName returns nil for an unmeasured code. The finding's suggested red->yellow degrade was NOT adopted: the shipped WRITE_ONLY_NEAREST={red=1} is a deliberate later refinement that is better, because yellow is a real Kobo colour and would misreport the highlight, while pink names what the device actually shows. Verified on main at 0b8c2d02d.
